# Package list reflects shared seat availability, one-seat wording, and fully booked actions

> Prove the package comparison page shows the fixed package set, package-card features, seat-capacity messaging, and the correct action for packages with plural remaining seats, exactly one remaining seat, and no seats left.

## Step 1

Open http://127.0.0.1:5050/publish in browser session A and keep the page available for the shared-seat check.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-21, ac-22, ac-25, ac-27, ac-28, ac-29, ac-30, ac-31

Open http://127.0.0.1:5050/publish in a second isolated browser session B, review the package cards, then assert there are exactly four cards for Starter, Standard, Premium, and Author's Choice; each card shows its specified price and turnaround and a feature list; every package card that currently has seats remaining shows a seats-left message and `Choose <package name>`; and the Author's Choice card shows `Fully booked this month` with `View details` and no `Choose Author's Choice`.

## Step 3

In browser session A, from http://127.0.0.1:5050/publish open the Premium package detail page and submit one valid manuscript with book title {{publish_test_book_title}}, author name {{publish_test_author_name}}, email {{publish_test_author_email}}, genre Mystery, manuscript status New Manuscript, and any available Premium onboarding seat.

## Step 4 @verifies ac-23, ac-26

Back in browser session B on http://127.0.0.1:5050/publish, refresh the package list after the Premium submission from session A, then assert the Premium card now shows `1 seat left this month`, proving the claimed seat changed the shared monthly pool seen by another visitor.

## Step 5

In browser session A, open http://127.0.0.1:5050/my-submissions and withdraw the Premium submission created in this test so the seat returns to the pool for later runs.

judgements.rationale: [self_critique] Oracle-to-promise fit was kept tight: the cross-session refresh observed the singular `1 seat left this month` state after a seat claim in another browser session, which directly proves both the shared-pool propagation and the one-seat boundary wording. I did not overclaim the exact total pool sizes here because that remains the declared gap **gap-5**.

[self_critique] Technique fit used equivalence partitioning across the four real packages because package identity changes displayed values but not the navigation flow. I avoided an over-broad single summary assert by giving each package detail page its own observation step with explicit code, price, turnaround, tagline, and features.

[self_critique] The negative path was kept as a distinct test so the suite includes explicit bad-resource coverage rather than only happy browsing. The final assert stayed narrow to HTTP 404 because the committed acceptance criterion did not specify any exact 404-page body text.

[self_critique] Negative coverage was present for the nonexistent package path and the fully booked list state, so no additional negative scenario was omitted under the current three-scenario budget. The main residual risk is observability of the fixed seat-cap totals, which stayed recorded as **gap-5** instead of being diluted into a weaker, misleading check.
